name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: IRGC claims six tankers hit mines near Hormuz since 15 Nov; UKMTO reported one tanker hit by a projectile on 16 Nov
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 16 Nov that six oil tankers had hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz since 15 Nov and were disabled or sunk; the claim has not been independently confirmed (Trend News Agency; The National). UKMTO reported one tanker struck by an unidentified projectile early on 16 Nov, with an engine-room fire and no casualties (Euronews). Iran has restricted the strait since July and the US blockades Iranian ports, so Hormuz traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Expect continued disruption and delays to Gulf shipping, with knock-on effects for fuel and freight costs. Mariners should follow UKMTO advisories for the region.

sources.title: Trend — IRGC says six tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
The National — Iran escalates threats as third US carrier arrives
Euronews — US and Iran slide closer to fresh all-out war

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
